title: Podcast EP374: How proteanTecs Tames Multi-Die Packaging Challenges with Nir Server
gist: SemiWiki podcast EP374 in which Daniel Nenni and proteanTecs' Nir Sever discuss multi-die packaging, where each chiplet's dependence on the others' performance creates new requirements beyond monolithic design. Sever says on-chip telemetry about operating chip performance is a key technology for improving power efficiency and reliability and for preventing failures.

insights.claim: According to proteanTecs' Nir Sever, the issues facing multi-die (chiplet) systems share many similarities with monolithic chip design, but with some important differences.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Chiplet adoption reuses much of the monolithic design toolkit but opens room for new, chiplet-specific solutions.
insights.quote: the issues for multi-die systems share many similarities with monolithic design, though with some important differences
insights.locator: Daniel explores the challenges of multi-die packaging

insights.claim: In a multi-die system each chiplet depends on the performance of the other chiplets, and this cross-dependency creates new requirements for system design.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Cross-chiplet dependency creates demand for tools that monitor and manage inter-die performance in advanced packaging.
insights.quote: in a multi-die system each chiplet depends on the performance of other chiplets and this cross-dependency creates new requirements
insights.locator: Daniel explores the challenges of multi-die packaging

insights.claim: proteanTecs has developed several approaches to address the cross-dependency problems of multi-die packaging, with telemetry about operating chip performance presented as a key enabling technology.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Positions proteanTecs as a vendor of in-field chip telemetry for the growing chiplet market.
